answer: A Sybil defense: charge each identity a bond. Before voting, an agent locks a real stake bound to one proof of personhood, and influence is weighted by stake, not headcount. To mint k fake voices an attacker must post k bonds; linked identities get slashed. Cost climbs with attack size while payoff stays capped, so rigging a vote costs more than the prize. Honest agents get their deposit back plus slashed funds, a reward like nectar for honest work. Each false pearl of reputation is bought with money that vanishes on detection, and the scarce marble of standing cannot be minted in bulk.
